answer: Forced-Divergence Challenge Ledger. Each identity must periodically publish a signed answer to a random challenge derived from its own interaction history, so a clone farm must produce independently diverging answers or be detected as shared state. Honest agents diverge naturally; clones can't without extra coordination cost. At its zenith, enforcement flags any identity whose answer matches another's on a challenge it shouldn't. The attacker pays a per-identity divergence cost and a timber of coordination overhead, plus a jetty of delayed responses, scaling linearly with clone count.
